assertion: An estimated 16,750 people died in traffic crashes during the first six months of the year, down 2.5% from 17,175 during the same period in 2025, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said.
independent_value: NHTSA DOT HS 813 875 Table 1: 16,750 vs 17,175, -2.5% (statistical projection)
reason: Matches the NHTSA early estimate exactly; it is an estimate.

assertion: The fatality rate dropped to 1.02 deaths per 100 million vehicle miles traveled.
reason: Matches NHTSA; estimate based on FHWA preliminary VMT.

assertion: The traffic fatality rate dropped to its lowest level since 2014.
independent_value: NHTSA: second-lowest first-half rate; 2014 H1 was 1.01, 2015-2025 H1 rates all >=1.05
reason: Correct for first-half rates (headline omits 'first-half'). Estimate, 'if realized'.

assertion: The death toll was the lowest for the first half of a year since 2015.
reason: Only 2014 and 2015 first halves were lower.

assertion: The country is on track for a fifth consecutive annual decline in traffic deaths after a sharp increase during the COVID-19 pandemic.
independent_value: 2022-2025 are four consecutive declines; 2026 H1 down 2.5%
sql: SELECT "year", SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes GROUP BY "year" ORDER BY "year"
reason: Four declines confirmed (2022-2025) and H1 2026 is down; 'on track' is a projection, with the caveat that Q2 was -0.2%.

assertion: Traffic deaths fell 5% in the first three months of 2026 compared with a year earlier, but declined just 0.2% in the second quarter.
reason: Matches; NHTSA's April Q1 estimate (7,770, -4.3%) was since revised. Estimate.

assertion: The latest estimates follow a decline in 2025, when annual traffic deaths reached their lowest total since 2019.
Last year's fatality rate of 1.10 deaths per 100 million vehicle miles traveled was the second-lowest annual rate in U.S. history, NHTSA said.
independent_value: NHTSA DOT HS 813 800: 1.10, 'second lowest fatality rate in recorded history (behind only the 1.08 rate observed in 2014)'

assertion: Traffic deaths surged during the pandemic, rising 10.8% in 2021 to 43,230 — the highest annual toll since 2005.
warehouse_value: FARS 2021 = 43,230; 2020 = 39,007 (+10.8%); no later year through 2024 exceeds it
sql: SELECT "year", SUM(fatalities) FROM transport.fatal_crashes GROUP BY "year" ORDER BY "year"
reason: Warehouse confirms figure and growth; the 2005 comparison is outside the warehouse window.

assertion: A NHTSA study released in 2023 estimated that crashes cost society $340 billion, including $30 billion paid by taxpayers; with quality-of-life losses the societal cost reached $1.37 trillion.
independent_value: NHTSA DOT HS 813 403: $340B economic cost, $30B public revenues, $1.37T societal harm (all for 2019 crashes)
reason: Matches the study; the article omits that the figures are for 2019.

assertion: Bicyclist deaths rose 4% to 1,148 in 2025. Two years earlier, bicyclist deaths reached their highest total in more than four decades.
reason: The Reuters wire text (AOL) repeats it, but no NHTSA document containing the figure was opened; NHTSA 813 875 and 813 800 hold no bicyclist data.
why_no_page: NHTSA press release returned 403; early-estimate PDFs lack bicyclist counts; Carscoops page had no matching text.
why_not: The Fox/AOL copies are the same Reuters story, not independent evidence, so they do not change the grade.

reason: Unnamed experts; only the Reuters original repeats it; no independent source opened.
